title: Add CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and warmup (fix regressions)
author: Ava Chen
description:
Introduce CUDA graph capture/replay path with runtime shape guards and a warmup priming flow. This change adds capture/replay APIs in the GPU runtime, protects replays with lightweight shape-guard checks to avoid silent correctness regressions when sequence lengths or batch shapes change, and implements an explicit warmup/priming path for KV cache and attention kernels. Motivation: CUDA graphs reduce kernel launch overhead and improve throughput/latency for steady-state token generation, but naive capture/replay caused regressions for workloads with dynamic sequence lengths and cold KV caches. This PR implements shape-aware guards and a small warmup flow to ensure correctness while preserving the perf benefits. Includes unit + integration tests and a benchmark harness for the capture path.

High level changes: capture/replay implementation, shape guard checks, warmup priming sequence for KV cache and attention kernels, scheduler hints for continuous batching when graph replay is active, metrics for graph hit/miss and warmup success. Addresses regression seen in SUP-789 and tracked in ENG-3421.

Checklist:
- [x] Capture/replay core implementation
- [x] Shape guard and fallback to non-graph path
- [x] Warmup priming flow for KV cache and attention kernels
- [x] Integration tests covering dynamic seqlen and batch changes
- [x] Microbenchmark + perf results attached
- [x] Documentation + runtime config flags

perf_summary: Benchmark: streaming generation, 16-token generations, batch size 8, A100 x2
Results: 9-12% improvement in p95 latency compared to baseline non-graph path, 15% increase in sustained throughput for steady-state token generation, negligible mem overhead (~2%)
Notes: benefits most visible for steady-state long-form generation. Short, highly dynamic seqlen workloads fall back to non-graph path and see no regression.
Regression fixes: fixed an OOB read when replayed graph saw shorter sequence length (addressed in commit f7b2d40); added warmup priming to avoid cold-KV stalls observed in SUP-789.

squash: Add CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and warmup

- capture/replay implementation
- shape guards and fallback path
- KV cache warmup priming
- scheduler hints and metrics
- tests and docs

Fixes: SUP-789, addresses ENG-3421
release_notes: Added optional CUDA graph capture/replay for GPU runtime (runtime.gpu.enable_cuda_graph_replay=true).
Added shape guards to ensure safe replay fallback for dynamic sequence lengths.
Introduced warmup priming to avoid cold-KV cache stalls; metrics exposed for graph_hit/graph_miss/warmup_success.
Performance: up to 12% p95 latency reduction and ~15% throughput improvement on steady-state generation workloads (A100).
